---
title: "How tests are reviewed"
description: "What Claude is shown, the quality rules, the safeguards for existing tests, and how failing tests are classified."
---

How the [test suggestions](test-suggest.qmd) decide what to propose. The
review uses a stronger Claude model than the
[roxygen suggestions](roxygen-suggest.qmd), with extended thinking:
deciding which tests add value, and why an existing test fails, needs more
careful reasoning than documentation.

## What Claude gets

Besides the function and all its [test files](test-suggest.qmd#test-files):

- **How your test files are named**, and for categories what each one
  means.
- **The results of the existing tests**, run before anything is changed.
- **The history**: when the function and each test file last changed, and
  in the changes under review (a PR or push) whether the function changed
  without its tests — with the diff.
- **Your test support files** (`tests/testthat/setup*.R`, `helper*.R`)
  and the files they `source()` verbatim, so the tests use your own
  objects, connection helpers and helper functions. Together they are
  capped at 60,000 characters; files beyond that are named, not shown.
- **For a function without tests**, one or two typical test files of
  other functions, as examples of how your package writes tests.
- **The structure of the test data** those files create: for each table
  its rows, columns, types and missing values, and for factors the counts
  per level. The level counts are the only data values sent to Claude.

## New tests

Claude names the value of each new test — an uncovered code path, error
handling, an edge case, or a likely regression. Tests without such a
reason are dropped, as are copies of existing tests (see
[what gets proposed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed)). Claude is asked
to write tests that

- assert **concrete values** from the known test data (counts, levels,
  dimensions), not just a class;
- always assert something — no `if (...) expect_...`;
- never swallow errors or warnings with `try()` / `tryCatch()`, but check
  them with `expect_error()` / `expect_warning()`;
- test each error branch once;
- describe exactly what they check.

## Existing tests {#existing-tests}

Claude also decides on existing tests, and states a reason for each:

| Action | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| Update | `contract_changed` | The function was changed on purpose and the test still expects the old behaviour |
| Delete | `duplicate`, `behavior_removed`, `trivial` | The test repeats another, tests something the function no longer does, or asserts nothing meaningful |
| Report | `possible_code_bug` | The test fails, and the code rather than the test looks wrong |

Safeguards apply before anything is changed:

- **Only a failing test is updated.** A passing test is never rewritten.
- **A test is never adapted to output that may be wrong.** If the code may
  be at fault, the test stays and is reported instead.
- **An update must pass a real run**; otherwise the original test is kept
  and the attempt is reported.

## Failing tests {#failing-tests}

A generated test that fails is not proposed. Where the error alone
decides — the test doesn't parse, calls a function that doesn't exist, or
needs a package that isn't installed — R classifies it; the other failures
of a function go to Claude in one call, with the actual error output.
Claude says why each failed, and how sure it is (high, medium, low):

| Classification | Meaning | Reported as |
|---|---|---|
| `real_bug` | The test is right and found a defect | A possible bug in the code: in the report, and at high confidence an issue |
| `bad_test` | The test itself is wrong | A comment on your PR |
| `env_misconfiguration` | The test setup is broken, e.g. a missing package | A comment on your PR |

- **Which possible bugs are reported** follows the
  `code-issue-confidence` input, else `possible_bugs` in
  `config/suggestion-policy.yml`: reported at high and medium
  confidence, an issue only at high.
- **One issue per function**, titled "Possible bug found by generated
  test: `<function>`". A new issue lists all failing tests of that run,
  each with its code folded away. While it is open, a later run adds only
  a short "still failing" comment with the test names.
- **Repeats are left out:** a test that failed in an earlier run (same
  name, or one Claude says it repeats) isn't classified, commented or
  filed again.
- **Without a pull request** (a push, scheduled or manual run, or a
  [full review](suggestions.qmd#full-review)) there is no PR to comment on,
  so the last two are listed in the suggestion PR's description instead,
  or in one issue if no test passed at all.

Where each kind of report goes can be changed, see
[where reports go](suggestions.qmd#where-reports-go).
